npcs.name: Mei Tanaka
npcs.greeting: Welcome to town! I'm Mei. I run Seed & Soil Co. If it grows, I probably sell the seeds for it.
lines: Organic produce always sells better. People can taste the difference.
Buy seeds for the season you're in. A tomato won't sprout in the snow!
Business is slow on rainy days. Good for your crops, though.
You're becoming one of my best suppliers!
I saved you the good seed packets. The ones from last year's best plants.
My grandmother said: feed the soil, not the plant.
Honestly, the town feels more alive since you moved in.
I'm thinking of adding a whole shelf just for your harvest.
You're not just a customer anymore. You're a friend.

stories.text: Can I tell you something? I almost closed the shop last year. Nobody was farming anymore. Then you showed up.
My grandmother started this shop with one shelf of seeds she saved herself. I still keep her seed jars in the back. Want to see them sometime?
I've decided: the best produce shelf gets a sign with your farm's name on it. Don't argue!

npcs.name: Dr. Amara Okafor
npcs.greeting: Hello! I'm Dr. Okafor, the county soil scientist. Bring me your questions. And your dirt!
lines: A teaspoon of healthy soil can hold more living things than there are people on Earth.
Test before you treat. Lime only helps if your soil is actually acidic.
Organic matter is like a sponge. More of it means your soil holds more water.
Your soil tests are getting better. I can see it in the numbers!
Fungi threads can stretch for miles underground, connecting plant roots.
Every time you till, you break the soil's crumbs. Try to till only what you plant.
You think like a scientist now. Observe, test, then act.
I'd like to write up your farm as a case study, if you don't mind.
When I started, the community garden was the best soil in the county. You could make it that way again.

stories.text: I grew up on a farm where the topsoil had blown away. That's why I became a soil scientist: so no one else loses their land that way.
Do you know what I love most about soil? It's the most alive place on Earth, and almost nobody looks at it.
I'm presenting your farm's soil data at the state conference. You're turning worn-out ground into living soil. People need to see that it's possible.

npcs.name: June Hale

schedule.doing: asleep early. Bees start at dawn!

npcs.greeting: Oh, hello! Careful, the bees are busy. I'm June. If it buzzes, flutters, or crawls, I can tell you its name.
lines: A honeybee visits about a hundred flowers on one trip.
Plant some flowers near your crops. The bees will thank you with better harvests.
Ladybugs eat aphids by the dozen. Never spray them!
Have you filled in your Nature Journal? I'd love to see it.
Clover is a bee's favorite snack. And it feeds the soil too!
Fog brings out the mushrooms. Just look, never eat, unless an expert says so.
You notice things now. The little things. That's the whole secret.
My bees forage on your farm, you know. Your honey is partly mine!
I'm glad someone young is caring for this land.

stories.text: My first hive swarmed away. I cried for a week, then I read every bee book in the library. Mistakes are just lessons with stings attached.
Some evenings I just sit and listen to the hives. Thousands of bees, all humming together. It sounds like the whole valley breathing.
I've been keeping a journal of every creature on this land for forty years. When I'm too old for it, I'd like you to have it.

npcs.name: Luis Ortega
npcs.greeting: So you're the new farmer! Luis Ortega. My family's been growing corn here for three generations.
lines: Corn, beans, and squash grow great together. The 'Three Sisters,' my abuela called them.
Watch the forecast. One frost can wipe out a whole field of beans.
Rotate your crops. Same crop, same spot, same pests.
Your field is looking good, neighbor!
I tried your no-till idea. Fewer weeds than I expected!
Pip won't stop talking about your farm.
You're family now. Come for dinner anytime.
Between your farm and mine, this valley is coming back to life.
Abuela would've liked you.

stories.text: When the dust storms came in my grandfather's time, they plowed everything bare. We lost half our soil. My abuela planted cover crops to bring it back.
I used to think farming was just about yields. Watching your farm, I'm starting to think it's about the soil first.
Pip wants to take over the farm someday. Because of you, I think there'll still be good soil left for them.

npcs.name: Pip Ortega

schedule.doing: looking for frogs in the fountain

npcs.greeting: Whoa, you're the new farmer?! I'm Pip! Do worms have eyes? Do YOU know?
lines: Why is dirt brown? Is it rusty?
If you cut a worm in half do you get two worms? (Dad says no.)
I found a pill bug! It rolled into a ball! Is it a bug or a shrimp??
I counted 7 worms in one shovel of dirt! Is that good?
Why do leaves change color in fall? Where does the green go?
Can I help on your farm someday?
When I grow up I'm going to be a soil scientist like Dr. Okafor!
You're the coolest grown-up I know. Don't tell Dad.
I made you a rock. It's a good rock.

stories.text: I made a list of every bug I've ever found. It has 47 bugs on it. Okay, 12 are the same pill bug. His name is Gerald.
Dr. Okafor let me look at dirt under a microscope! There were tiny worms called nematodes! They were WIGGLING!
When I'm a soil scientist I'm going to name a microbe after you. A good one. Not a stinky one.

quests.title: Meet the neighbors
quests.ask: Have you met everyone yet? Say hi to all five of us. Small town, big hearts!
quests.thanks: Now you know everyone! Here's a little welcome gift from all of us.

quests.title: A neighborly trade
quests.ask: My carrot patch got eaten by rabbits. Could you spare 5 carrots? I'll make it worth your while.
quests.thanks: Gracias! These look great. Take some seeds from my stash.

quests.title: Know your soil
quests.ask: Before you change your soil, measure it. Run all three tests (lab kit, shovel, and infiltration ring) on 3 garden spots.
quests.thanks: Excellent data! Now you can see what your soil needs instead of guessing. That's science.

quests.title: Sweeten sour soil
quests.ask: Most of the soil around here is a little acidic. Bring one tested spot up to pH 6.2 or higher. Lime does it, and compost helps too.
quests.thanks: pH 6.2! Now phosphorus and other nutrients can actually reach the roots.

steps.label: Raise a tested spot to pH 6.2+

quests.title: Little red helpers
quests.ask: Have you seen a lady beetle on your farm yet? They're the best pest control there is. Find one for your Nature Journal.
quests.thanks: Isn't she lovely? Here, a bug hotel, so more of them move in.

quests.title: Worm detective
quests.ask: Dad says worms mean good dirt. Can you find one with your shovel? Do a shovel test!
quests.thanks: A WORM! You found a worm! Okay this rock is for you. It's my second-best rock.

steps.label: Find an earthworm with a shovel test

quests.title: Chasing rainbows
quests.ask: I want to see a rainbow! When do they happen? Tell me when you see one!
quests.thanks: Sun behind you, rain in front! I'm going to stand in the right spot next time.

quests.title: Food for the bees
quests.ask: My bees need more flowers. Could you grow sunflowers and bring me 3? I'll share something special.
quests.thanks: Look at those faces! My bees will be so happy. Take this hive: you've earned it.

quests.title: The Three Sisters
quests.ask: My abuela grew corn, beans, and squash together. The corn holds up the beans, the beans feed the soil, and the squash shades out weeds. Bring me 3 of each, grade C or better, and I'll show you her recipe.
quests.thanks: Just like Abuela's garden. You understand this land now.

steps.label: Bring 3 corn, 3 beans, and 3 squash (grade C+)

quests.title: The perfect tomato
quests.ask: A customer wants the best tomato in the county. Grade A or better. Think your soil is up to it?
quests.thanks: That's a beauty! Healthy soil really does grow better food.

steps.label: Bring Mei a grade A tomato

quests.title: Restore the community garden
quests.ask: The community garden behind the square used to be the best soil in the county. Help me bring it back? Clear it, feed it, and plant a cover crop to heal it.
quests.thanks: Look at it! Living soil again. The whole town owes you one, and the garden is yours to farm too.

steps.label: Clear weeds, sticks, and stones from the community garden
Bring Dr. Okafor 6 compost for the garden
Plant clover on 6 community garden spots
